newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia bond ylds drop, anticipate friendly data.
newsitem.headline: Australia bond ylds drop, anticipate friendly data.

text.p: *Australian bond yields ended lower, although some
cautionary profit-taking ahead of the U.S. CPI later on Tuesday saw them just above their early lows.
*Market makes strong outperformance against the U.S.

Australian bonds yields were sharply lower in anticipation that key local data over the next couple of weeks will be friendly, and shaking off the anxiety over Federal Reserve policy which continues to dog the U.S..

Domestic bond futures saw a dramatic short squeeze just after the start as the market continued to reprice itself against the U.S. on the expectataion the Reserve Bank will not follow the Fed into a tightening cycle for some months to come.
However, some cautionary profit-taking ahead of the March U.S. CPI later on Tuesday saw the rally pared slightly, although the market put in a strong outperformance against the U.S..

"I think people should be cautious chasing the rally at the longer end," said Stephen Roberts, chief economist at UBS Australia. "When it rallies into the high seven's (percent), there's not an awful lot of value there unless you get dramatically improved inflation results."

However, analysts, including Roberts, expect a benign outcome to next week's quarterly CPI report, and if this is followed by subdued wages data, they are not ruling out a policy easing by the RBA in the wake of last week's weak jobs report.
Early futures buying was across the curve, and saw bill futures pushing out expectations of a tightening.
Recent volatility in equities and bonds is also seeing some funds diverting some of their portfolios to the short end, which is causing a shortage in the bill market, traders said.

June bill futures continued a recent uptrend to around 94.00, bringing the contract back into line with current official 6.0 percent rates, and been discounting a 25 basis point tightening just over a month ago.

Meanwhile, all eyes will be on the March core U.S. CPI later on Tuesday, which is forecast to rise 0.3 percent, as the core PPI last Friday unnerved the U.S. market after jumping an unexpected 0.4 percent.

The local rally saw the Australian/U.S. 10-year spread narrow to the low 90s at one stage, its lowest level since mid-February. N.Z. bonds outshone the bloc following much weaker than expected March quarter inflation. The RBNZ said underlying inflation was 0.22 percent against a forecast 0.5 percent.
The early squeeze saw the 10-year bond contract overcome resistance at 92.010, but failed to sustain the move above 92.050 and towardd last week's 92.080 peak.
